rankingBasis: Ordinal information gain per material/measurement burden; not probabilities, discovery claims or a record of completed experiments.

hypotheses.title: Coupled coils exchange and dissipate supplied energy
hypotheses.prediction: Changing secondary loading changes both receiver output and transmitter response under a passive coupled-circuit model.
hypotheses.rival: Apparent excess is an omitted source, stored energy, mutual-energy term or voltage/current phase error.
hypotheses.observable: Signed input power; primary/secondary currents; stored-field energy; load and copper loss.
hypotheses.falsifier: Energy closure fails outside declared numerical or measurement uncertainty after every term is retained.
hypotheses.novelty: Established model; new project application and adversarial controls, not a new conservation law.

hypotheses.title: Receiver loading can help localize a drive
hypotheses.prediction: Complex responses across deliberately changed loads can distinguish drives at different ports when the transfer columns are independent.
hypotheses.rival: Unknown coupling, distributed pickup or gain can reproduce a source-location signature.
hypotheses.observable: Amplitude and phase at two ports across loads and frequencies; conditioning of the inference map.
controls: Fit one load and predict another
materials: Optional low-voltage generator and synchronous readout
hypotheses.falsifier: A rival drive/gain pair reproduces every selected observable or a held-out load defeats the inferred source.
hypotheses.novelty: Potentially useful apparatus-specific inference experiment; novelty not established.
hypotheses.executionBoundary: The across-load prediction is a future extension. Frozen R2 tests a coherent two-current inversion at one frequency and nominal load, with parameter and phase uncertainty; it does not execute a load scan.

hypotheses.title: A dark-matter-like narrow line needs environmental witnesses
hypotheses.prediction: A specified hypothetical signal response must survive appropriate source-field and environmental-control comparisons with retained sensitivity.
hypotheses.rival: Mains harmonics, moving spectral lines, gain drift or magnetic vibration make similar peaks.
hypotheses.observable: Calibrated transfer function, line evolution and witness cross-response; no cosmological identification from peak shape alone.
hypotheses.falsifier: A supposed identifying statistic can be reproduced by an ordinary nuisance or rejects injected signals.
hypotheses.novelty: Control-design exercise; not an axion search or a claim of achieved particle sensitivity.

hypotheses.title: Readout sensitivity has an optimum that need not maximize signal amplitude
hypotheses.prediction: In a stated noisy receiver model, stronger coupling alters loading and input-referred noise as well as gain.
hypotheses.rival: Ranking designs by peak voltage hides backaction, bandwidth loss or added inductance.
hypotheses.observable: Signal-to-noise metric and transfer bandwidth under fixed source/noise assumptions.
hypotheses.falsifier: The purported optimum changes when omitted noise/bandwidth is included or fails held-out parameter tests.
hypotheses.novelty: Classical analogue only unless quantum/SQUID assumptions are explicitly implemented.

hypotheses.title: A scale signal is not automatically a change in gravity
hypotheses.prediction: Ordinary electromagnetic lift changes a sample support force and produces a reaction elsewhere in the apparatus.
hypotheses.rival: Lead forces, susceptibility, electrostatic attraction, heating or source support outside the weighed boundary.
hypotheses.observable: Sample and source reaction; field gradient; separately characterized reference.
materials: Later magnet/coil, stand and force/position sensors
hypotheses.falsifier: The signal follows material/field geometry or cancels with source reaction; remaining unexplained residual does not identify gravity.
hypotheses.novelty: Known physical alternatives; no bench gravity result.

hypotheses.title: Prism geometry can distinguish dispersion from a single-index optical model
hypotheses.prediction: With stipulated wavelength-dependent indices, a two-prism ray model predicts different emergent angles for selected spectral rays.
hypotheses.rival: Single-index model, aperture extent or geometry misalignment explains an apparent spread.
hypotheses.observable: Ray intersection positions and angular separations under declared indices and geometry.
materials: Optional prism, diffuse white light and screen
hypotheses.falsifier: The variable-index model fails its own geometric constraints or a competing calibrated model fits the chosen observations.
hypotheses.novelty: Modern illustrative reconstruction; stipulated colors/indices are not historical measurements.

hypotheses.title: Orbital periods identify force scaling only under stated geometry
hypotheses.prediction: For circular trajectories, T² proportional to r³ implies centripetal acceleration proportional to r^-2.
hypotheses.rival: Different orbit geometry, period definition or an unmodeled central distribution changes the inverse interpretation.
hypotheses.observable: Period-radius log slope and forward trajectory agreement.
hypotheses.falsifier: A claimed general force law cannot reproduce held-out trajectories, or multiple laws remain observationally indistinguishable.
hypotheses.novelty: Established reconstruction; no inference of dark matter from a toy orbit.

hypotheses.title: A chymical name and color do not uniquely identify an element
hypotheses.prediction: Context and independent composition/phase information narrow a set of plausible modern substances more than the symbol alone.
hypotheses.rival: Literal universal substitution of every planetary name by one pure element.
hypotheses.observable: Candidate-set size and contradictions against source context.
materials: Reference data; no preparation of historical mixtures
hypotheses.falsifier: A proposed unique identification fails another occurrence or an independent assay; unresolved candidates remain plural.
hypotheses.novelty: Source-bound classification, not transmutation or a measured historical composition.

hypotheses.title: Collected radiant energy must be traced to an external flux or initial storage
hypotheses.prediction: A powered/light-driven charging analogue supplies output only through tracked input and stored energy.
hypotheses.rival: Uncounted light, auxiliary supply or charged capacitor is called source-free output.
hypotheses.observable: Incident-input proxy, charging history, delivered joules and endpoint storage.
hypotheses.falsifier: Output attributed to a novel source disappears when external/initial energy is counted; an anomaly requires an uncertainty-bounded physical budget.
hypotheses.novelty: Conceptual analogue, not replication of Tesla radiation hardware.

hypotheses.title: Static diamagnetic lift has a geometric restoring-force signature
hypotheses.prediction: A declared diamagnetic model predicts an equilibrium where magnetic force balances weight and a geometry-dependent local stiffness.
hypotheses.rival: Optical parallax, airflow, supports, unmodeled susceptibility anisotropy or finite-magnet geometry.
hypotheses.observable: Equilibrium gap, displacement response and stiffness.
materials: Later contained magnets and pre-cut graphite
hypotheses.falsifier: The model misses held-out equilibria or stability within its declared approximation error.
hypotheses.novelty: Magnetic support, not gravity shielding; no claim of free mechanical work.

hypotheses.title: Internal moving masses require a complete center-of-mass test
hypotheses.prediction: In an isolated Newtonian model, cyclic internal actuation preserves total momentum; supported devices may move through environmental reactions.
hypotheses.rival: Tracking the housing while omitting moving masses, friction, cables or expelled material creates apparent reactionless motion.
hypotheses.observable: Center-of-mass trajectory of housing plus every moving mass and source.
hypotheses.falsifier: An asserted isolated translation vanishes with the complete boundary, or model momentum fails numerical convergence.
hypotheses.novelty: A new patent motivates a standard conservation audit; no hardware performance validated.

hypotheses.title: Asymmetric electrostatic pressure must close the force boundary
hypotheses.prediction: A declared static apparatus model includes all electrodes, source and external boundaries in its force integral.
hypotheses.rival: Partial surface integration, chamber attraction, gas momentum or leakage is interpreted as a self-force.
hypotheses.observable: Closed/partial stress integral and dependence on boundary placement.
hypotheses.falsifier: The alleged closed-system thrust disappears with omitted surfaces or environmental exchange; a residual alone is not inertial-mass reduction.
hypotheses.novelty: No independently validated exotic mechanism selected; no high-voltage build.

hypotheses.title: Newton’s 2060 date depends on an interpretive chronology
hypotheses.prediction: Changing a chosen historical starting date shifts a day/year-derived endpoint by the same amount.
hypotheses.rival: A theological bound is presented as a unique successful physical forecast.
hypotheses.observable: Explicit starting date, time-unit interpretation and endpoint; manuscript qualification retained.
hypotheses.falsifier: The claim of a unique physical prediction fails when its interpretive premises are exposed; theological truth is not adjudicated by a circuit test.
hypotheses.novelty: Historical sensitivity analysis; no probability or countdown to an apocalypse.

hypotheses.title: A Hermetic correspondence becomes physics only after a testable map is specified
hypotheses.prediction: If two models are claimed equivalent, an explicit state/observable map must preserve the declared dynamics within a bounded error.
hypotheses.rival: Visual similarity or an above/below metaphor substitutes for units, boundary conditions and an identifying prediction.
hypotheses.observable: Mapped trajectories or conserved quantities, plus residual error over a declared domain.
controls: Counterexample with similar appearance but different dynamics
hypotheses.falsifier: A map fails a held-out boundary or cannot be defined; retain the idea as interpretation rather than a physical law.
hypotheses.novelty: Modern methodological reconstruction, not a theorem attributed to Newton or Hermes.

hypotheses.title: Astronomical calculation and astrological prediction need separate validation
hypotheses.prediction: A numerical ephemeris can match reference geometry while a separately fixed symbolic rule has no established outcome-prediction score.
hypotheses.rival: Correct planet coordinates or consistent rule execution are treated as evidence for destiny/occult causation.
hypotheses.observable: Coordinate error separately from a preregistered, blinded predictive score against a base-rate model.
hypotheses.falsifier: A claimed predictive improvement fails out-of-sample or disappears after leakage/base-rate controls; a synthetic demonstration supplies no empirical endorsement.
hypotheses.novelty: No human-outcome study performed; existing tools serve historical study and geometry.
